what: judo.sh generate-root failed with a Maven daemon connect timeout because the mvnd registry file was corrupt.
why: Corrupt ~/.m2/mvnd/registry/1.0.2/registry.bin (Bad string size). Local tooling state, not a catalog topic.
workaround: Killed mvnd processes, deleted registry.bin, reran generate-root.

what: generate-root stopped with 'manual changes in generated files' on .gitignore after the generated project was copied into the existing repo.
why: The builder copied the generator output over the repo's tracked .gitignore, so the generator saw a hand edit. The catalog does not say how to adopt generated files into a repo that already has its own .gitignore.
workaround: Restored the generated .gitignore, added .pi/dashboard/kb/ to .git/info/exclude, reran generate-root (exit 0).

what: Ran create-judo-project in /tmp/gen and copied the output into ~/Projects/webshop-test.
why: The target folder already held FUNCTIONS.md and git history. The catalog does not say whether create-judo-project may run in a non-empty repo or which folder to use.
workaround: cp -a of /tmp/gen into the repo, then merged .gitignore by hand.

what: The catalog gives the create-judo-project goal and its parameters but not the plugin groupId or version. The builder took version 1.0.0.20260311 from ~/.m2, which then pulled template 1.0.0.20261109 from judo-ng.
why: Build-process section lists parameters only. Plugin coordinates and a version pin are not documented, so the builder guessed from the local Maven cache.
workaround: Used the locally cached plugin version found under ~/.m2/repository/hu/blackbelt/judo.

what: The CLI doc says the judo-cli.jar is downloaded by ./judo.sh build. In this generated project, generate-root did not create target/judo-cli.jar. Running mvn -DgenerateRoot validate did.
why: The catalog describes the download as part of judo.sh build. The generated root pom has its own download-cli profile that runs on generateRoot, so the catalog is incomplete for the new-project case.
workaround: Ran mvn -B -DgenerateRoot validate, which copied target/judo-cli.jar.

what: Guessed the ESM type name Namespace in a query and got an error.
why: Type name was not checked against the metamodel before the query. Minor.
workaround: Queried the real types (Model, Package, StringType, NumericType) instead.

what: Mapping a TransferObjectType to an entity made the CLI auto-create members, forms, tables and views. The builder's hand-added DataMembers then failed validate --strict with binding and uniqueness errors.
why: The catalog does not say that a mapped TransferObjectType creates its members and UI scaffolds, so the builder assumed it had to create them.
workaround: Discarded the unsaved edits and rebuilt the model without the hand-added MAPPED members.

what: ActorType create warned that realm does not apply, because the actor was effectively anonymous.
why: The builder left anonymous unset while setting a realm. The accesspoint doc says realm applies only when the actor is not anonymous.
workaround: Second update set realm, managed=false and kind on webshop::Shop; the warning went away.

what: managed=true on an actor principal is meant to insert the principal row at first login, but the runtime does not do this. An AuthenticationInterceptor is needed.
why: The advanced-modeling pattern doc warns that auto-insert is not implemented in the current runtime, and the JIT best-practice confirms it.
workaround: Builder set managed=false and planned the row differently (see c01-11 and c01-45).

what: A Keycloak user and the application's actor row are two separate stores. The runtime needs both before it can resolve the actor.
why: Stated by the builder in its seed script header. Matches the catalog's Keycloak Users and the Entity Store section.

what: No documented recipe for the first login user of a local dev app: no test user, no seed data and no credentials are given for the generated Keycloak realm.
why: Grep of agent-docs found only integration-test users and the test realm file. The local-development doc has no login step. The builder had to create a Keycloak user and a DB row by hand.
workaround: Created Keycloak user shop/shop through the admin REST API and inserted a t_webshop_shop_user row with psql. Wrapped in scripts/seed-dev-user.sh.

what: The builder improvised the first-user fix before searching the kb. Its final report said the catalog had no recipe, then the kb search found the JIT provisioning doc and the platform behaviour section.
why: The kb-first habit was not applied at the start. The catalog did cover the row side (AuthenticationInterceptor JIT), though not the Keycloak user side.
workaround: Recorded as GAPS 15a after the user asked for kb-first on problems.

what: local-development.md gives the app URL as http://localhost:8181/apps/. The app is at /webshop/Shop/, and /apps/ only lists bundles.
why: Doc is out of date for the generated app path.
workaround: Used http://localhost:8181/webshop/Shop/ (from the Karaf start log).

what: Keycloak on the local port is served under /auth (Keycloak 23 with a relative path). Root and /realms return 404, and the catalog gives http://localhost:8080 with no path.
why: judo.sh starts Keycloak with --http-relative-path /auth, which the local-development doc does not mention.
workaround: Used http://localhost:8280/auth for admin and realm calls.

what: Port 8080 was already in use by another project's container, so Keycloak failed to take the default port.
why: Local environment conflict. The catalog does document keycloak_port as an override.
workaround: Set keycloak_port=8280 in judo.properties instead of the -o start option.

what: The generated judo.properties sets dbtype=hsqldb, but local-development.md says the default run uses PostgreSQL in Docker.
why: Doc and generated default disagree.
workaround: Changed dbtype to postgresql in judo.properties.

what: The predefined Text type is limited to 250 characters, which is too short for a product description. The catalog does not say so and does not name a long-text type.
why: Type doc lists StringType widget properties but not the Text length limit.
workaround: Added StringType LongText with maxLength 4000 in webshop::types.

what: No model-level way to show a price with two decimals in the generated table. The table shows 89.9 and 129.5.
why: The generated table valueFormatter uses Intl.NumberFormat with defaults. formatValue exists in the model but the table column does not set fraction digits.
workaround: Patched the generated table component (see c01-21).

what: The table column customizer example in table-hooks.md uses a (original) => ... signature and registration that do not match the shipped type, which is () => ColumnCustomizer.
why: Docs out of date against utilities/table.ts in the generated app.
workaround: Not used. Builder edited generated code instead.

what: After the generated table was patched and listed in .generator-ignore, ./judo.sh build -f failed with 'manual changes' on many generated frontend files (App.tsx, auth files, components). Only build -f -i passed.
why: Generator checksum check is not satisfied by the module .generator-ignore entry, so every changed or unlisted generated file blocks the frontend build. -i disables the check and refreshes checksums, which also hides real manual edits.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh build -f -i, later ./judo.sh build -M -B -i.

what: Patched one generated table component to use min and max fraction digits of 2, and listed the file in the frontend module .generator-ignore.
why: No model-level or documented hook produced 2 decimals, and the builder judged a one-file patch the quickest path to S04.
workaround: Interim one-off fix; later orchestrator reverted it in Round 1.

what: Browser automation clicks and fills often did not reach the page. The builder then blamed slow app response and used many fixed waits and DOM eval clicks to move around.
why: Agent-browser tool problem. Refs went stale on re-render, text selectors failed, and clicks sent no events in several cases. Not an app latency issue.
workaround: Fixed waits (10 to 40 s), DOM eval clicks, direct location.hash changes, REST curl for data checks.

what: Creating a product through the browser form failed with 400 MISSING_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTE, while the same create by REST succeeded.
why: Browser fill and keyboard input did not commit the numeric Price field (values were shown in the field but not in the React state). Evidence points to the tool, not the app.
workaround: Checked S03 with curl REST calls instead of the form.

what: Said the app was slow to respond (15 to 40 s per click). The orchestrator later showed the server answers in milliseconds.
why: Wrong diagnosis from unreliable browser clicks; no curl timing was done to check.
workaround: Kept the fixed waits.

what: kb_get returned 'not found' for paths that kb_search had just listed, so the builder could not read those docs.
why: Path resolution in the kb tool fails for some listed sections; index refresh was still running at the time.
workaround: Read search snippets, or grepped the catalog directly.

what: The kb read guard fired about 25 times with 'consecutive searches without consulting the knowledge base' while the builder read catalog files with bash and read.
why: Guard counts source reads as searches. It nagged on every bash call that touched the catalog.
workaround: Ignored; some turns then used kb_search.

what: Context-mode replaced long bash output with a search summary, so Maven and log output could not be read directly. The builder had to write output to files and read them.
why: Output summarising in ctx_search hid the lines the builder needed for the first Maven run.
workaround: Redirected output to /tmp/wsout files and read them with read.

what: kb_search results were fragmented and marked stale while the index was still refreshing.
why: Index refresh was running at the start of the session.
workaround: Re-ran searches later.

what: Builder read the catalog through bash grep, sed and read for most of the first hour, instead of kb_search and kb_get. This is why the kb call share was low.
why: No kb-first rule was in the first prompt (the user later added it at line 723).
workaround: User steering at L723 and L756 changed the habit.

what: Builder ran validate, curl, log reads and browser checks between build steps. The user then said to check only at the end and to use kb for every question.
why: Check-as-you-go habit; the first prompt asked only for a final check.
workaround: Accepted the user rule at L906 and L907 for later rounds.

what: Shell commands used on macOS: GNU 'timeout' is not installed, and a find / scan timed out after 60 s.
why: Builder assumed a Linux shell and ran a whole-disk find.
workaround: Dropped timeout and ran Maven directly.

what: Paths under /tmp failed in the read tool (ENOENT) because the path resolves to /private/tmp on macOS.
why: Tool path handling for the macOS /tmp symlink.
workaround: Read the /private/tmp path or used bash cat.

what: judo.sh stop did not stop the foreground judo.sh start process or Karaf. The builder killed the leftover processes by PID.
why: Start was run under nohup and stop only tears down the Docker services and not the Karaf child.
workaround: pkill on judo.sh start and console.out, then restart.

what: After a frontend-only rebuild, Karaf still served the old frontend bundle from application/.karaf/system. The builder had to delete application/.karaf and restart.
why: Unpacked Karaf assembly was not refreshed by build -f; the old jar stayed in .karaf/system.
workaround: rm -rf application/.karaf, then build -i and start.

what: Karaf log after a restart showed NoClassDefFoundError for EolExecutionContext in the RDBMS OSGi bundle.
why: Unknown; the builder saw it and did not pursue it. Login and data still worked.

what: The frontend uses a hash router. Pages open at /webshop/Shop/#/Shop/Products/..., so direct paths without the hash return 404. The catalog does not mention this.
why: Frontend docs do not describe the router type or the URL shape.
workaround: Used hash URLs (for example #/Shop/Products/AccessTablePage).

what: Karaf startup prints 'Visit http://localhost:8181/api-spec/webshop', but that URL returns 404.
why: Startup log link does not match the served API spec path (the REST root is under /api/).
workaround: Used REST paths from the generated frontend services.

what: The REST contract for updates and lists is not documented: the paths under /api/webshop/Shop/Shop/..., the X-Judo-SignedIdentifier and X-Judo-Mask headers, and the ~list and ~update verbs.
why: Builder had to read the generated frontend services to find the update path and headers.
workaround: Read ProductInfoServiceImpl.ts and headers.ts, then called REST with curl.

what: A stale view-page identifier from before a restart gave INVALID_IDENTIFIER (400) in the browser, and the console showed Axios errors.
why: Signed identifiers become invalid after a restart. The catalog covers this in the Identifier Signing and signed identifier sections.
workaround: Cleared localStorage and sessionStorage and went back to the list.

what: The generated table does not open the view page on a row click in a way the builder could find. The only row-click doc was the e2e test helper, and the embedded table row view button applies to references.
why: The catalog has no section on how a TransferObjectTable opens its view page (rowOperations versus row click).
workaround: Used a DOM eval to click the grid cell, which opened the view page.

what: Clicked Back on a view page opened directly by URL. Back did nothing, because the breadcrumb stack was empty.
why: Breadcrumb navigation records only in-app navigation. The builder expected browser history.
workaround: Re-ran the path list to view, then Back, which worked.

what: validate --strict failed with ExposedTransferObjectTableHasColumns (no columns on the viewable table). The fix was the fill command, which the builder found by trial.
why: The accesspoint doc states the rule, but the fill command is not in the judo-cli reference (openspec sweep item MO-172 lists it as missing).
workaround: fill webshop::ProductInfo --pages view,form,table.

what: Tried create -t MenuItemAccess, which the CLI rejects because MenuItemAccess is created automatically for an actor's access.
why: Builder tried the create command on an auto-generated element.
workaround: Used create -t Access on the actor and let the CLI create the menu access.

what: Build log showed ERROR lines for com.sun:tools systemPath ${tools.jar} but BUILD SUCCESS was reported.
why: Generated pom uses a relative system path for tools.jar. Noise, not a failure.

what: Modelled the shop login as EntityType ShopUser (username is identifier), a ShopUserInfo transfer object mapped to it, and ActorType Shop with principal ShopUserInfo and managed=false.
why: Managed auto-insert is not implemented in this runtime (advanced-modeling-patterns), so the principal row must come from elsewhere.

what: Price is a NumericType with precision 12 and scale 2. LongText is a StringType with maxLength 4000. Product has name, description and price members.
why: Price needs two decimals; the predefined Text type is too short for a description.

what: Set dbtype=postgresql and keycloak_port=8280 in judo.properties, and committed them.
why: Local-development says the default is PostgreSQL in Docker, and port 8080 was taken.

what: Wrote scripts/seed-dev-user.sh (idempotent Keycloak user shop/shop plus the ShopUser row) instead of building a JIT AuthenticationInterceptor, because the interceptor adds backend code beyond Level 0.
why: Level 0 scope. The JIT best practice explains the interceptor, but the builder judged it out of scope.

what: Checked S03 create and update with curl REST calls rather than the browser form.
why: Browser form did not commit numeric input (see c01-23). The later user rule asked for checks only at the end.

what: Project scaffolded from the ESM fullstack template, CLI jar obtained, shop frame model built, app built and started, login to the shop home page verified in the browser.
why: Level 0 frame.
workaround: Manual Keycloak user and ShopUser row (c01-11).

what: Product entity with name (String), description (LongText) and price (Price, NumericType scale 2). Product form shows Price, Name and Description.
why: S02 acceptance.

what: ProductInfo transfer object on the Shop access (createable, updateable). Create and update checked by REST: Running shoe 89.90 changed to 79.90, plus Trail backpack and Wool socks. Browser create not reliable.
why: S03 acceptance.
workaround: curl instead of UI (c01-23).

what: Product list (table) shows name and price. Price column shows two decimals after the generated table was patched and rebuilt.
why: S04 acceptance.
workaround: Patched generated table component (c01-21).

what: Product view and edit page shows name, price and multi-line description. Back verified only after in-app navigation (list, row, view, Back).
why: S05 acceptance. The builder's first Back check was invalid (page opened by URL).
workaround: DOM eval clicks and hash navigation (c01-22, c01-41).

what: Data persisted across ./judo.sh stop and start: products still listed after restart (Running shoe 79.9, Wool socks, Trail backpack).
why: S06 acceptance.
workaround: Needed manual process kill and rm -rf application/.karaf (c01-33, c01-34).
